knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(0,-8)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(-3,-5)$ and $(-10,-2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes which are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-3,-5)$ and $(-10,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-2-(-5)}{-10-(-3)} \\  & =\frac{3}{-7} \\  & =- \frac{3}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (- \frac{3}{7})=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{7}{3}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(0,-8).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-8) & =\frac{7}{3}(x-0) \\ y+8 & =\frac{7 x}{3} \\ y & =\frac{7 x}{3} - 8\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(-8,-8)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(6,-2)$ and $(-1,-7).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes which are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(6,-2)$ and $(-1,-7):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-7-(-2)}{-1-6} \\  & =\frac{-5}{-7} \\  & =\frac{5}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (\frac{5}{7})=-1\,⇒\,m=- \frac{7}{5}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(-8,-8).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-8) & =- \frac{7}{5}(x-(-8)) \\ y+8 & =- \frac{7}{5}(x+8) \\ y+8 & =- \frac{7 x}{5} - \frac{56}{5} \\ y & =- \frac{7 x}{5} - \frac{96}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(-6,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(-5,-5)$ and $(1,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-5,-5)$ and $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-(-5)}{1-(-5)} \\  & =\frac{1+5}{1+5} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (1)=-1\,⇒\,m=-1.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(-6,0).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =-1(x-(-6)) \\ y-0 & =- x - 6 \\ y & =- x - 6\end{aligned}
$$
